title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1968-10-12
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Behringer Ultramatch SRC2000 -> Samplitude Professional v9.11 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: An immaculate sound‑board capture of the Oct 12 1968 Avalon show, highlighted by a transcendent Dark Star, searing The Eleven and an epic Other One/​Cryptical jam.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑upgraded soundboard tape delivers crystal‑clear, balanced audio that lets every nuance of the band shine.  Musically the performance is often called “the best of the era,” with a 15‑minute Dark Star, a blistering Eleven, a monster Other One/​Cryptical sequence and a soaring New Potato Caboose.  Even without Pigpen’s organ the group sounds tight, inventive and utterly fire‑filled.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 60 reviews overwhelmingly praise both the performance (standout jams, legendary Dark Star) and the recording quality (Miller upgrade, crisp mix).  The few lower‑rated comments are minor and do not affect the overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Miller’s digitized soundboard is described as crystal‑clear, crisp, with superb stereo imaging (e.g., “scratching percussion in DS”).  Some reviewers note slight pitch correction but no drop‑outs or muffiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A classic late‑1968 set: a powerful first set that builds into an incendiary second set, highlighted by extended psychedelic jams and seamless transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for soaring lead guitar tone, overtones/feedback during Dark Star, blistering solos and emotive vocals.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for a thirteens‑style bass solo in New Potato and solid rhythmic foundation throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Commended for thick rhythm guitar sound and strong vocal on New Potato; occasional mention of his “great” contributions.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ is absent – reviewers miss him but note the show still works without his keyboards.
band_member_comments.Drums: Post‑drums jam described as heavy and intense; a few call the drum segment “somewhat rough,” but overall the percussion drives the jams.
